extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of classical philosophy / ethics (Aristotle)
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and analysis (Nicomachean Ethics Books VIII–IX) of what friendship is, its species (utility, pleasure, virtue), its varieties (kin, companions, husband/wife), causes of quarrels, rules for requital, and its relation to justice, self-love, and communal life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three kinds of friendship (utility, pleasure, goodness)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three kinds of Friendship: those based on utility, those based on pleasure, and those based on goodness/virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each kind has distinct motives and durability: friendships based on goodness are permanent and disinterested; those based on pleasure or utility are liable to break when the pleasurable or useful quality ceases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality vs inequality and proportionate friendship
rubrics_metrics.description: Friendship may be between equals or between superior and inferior; in dissimilar parties the proportionate (relative) equality equalises and preserves the Friendship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those who are equal should be equalised in friendship; those unequal should render friendship in proportion to superiority (e.g., respect to the better, profit to the needy). Failure to observe due proportion leads to quarrels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friendship is based on Communion/Shared life
rubrics_metrics.description: All Friendship is based upon Communion; many friendships (same city, tribe, crew) exist by right of some expressed or implied agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Friendships grounded in common life, agreements, or shared activities are especially cohesive; communion explains civic and group bonds as friendships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friendship of Kindred depends on parental/source relation
rubrics_metrics.description: Friendship of Kindred derives from parental relation: parents love children as part of themselves; children love parents as derived from them; closeness to source and time of relation affects strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parents know their offspring more and love from earliest moments; mothers often have stronger affection. Cousin/relative bonds vary by distance from the common ancestor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraternal friendship resembles companionship
rubrics_metrics.description: Fraternal Friendship is like that of Companions because brothers are equal, of similar age, dispositions, and have been brought up together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shared upbringing and nearness of age promote intimacy and mutual testing that secures fraternal bonds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Husband–Wife friendship: mixed motives and natural pairing
rubrics_metrics.description: Between Husband and Wife there is the same Friendship as in Aristocracy: the relation is determined by relative excellence; marriage combines profitable and pleasurable elements and is based on nature's pairing for household life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Family is prior and more necessary than the community; children act as a common good binding spouses; the friendship may be based on virtue if both are good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political forms affect extent of friendship and justice
rubrics_metrics.description: In deflected constitutional forms the principle of Justice and Friendship are smaller; in Despotism there is little or no Friendship; in Democracy friendships are most considerable because equals have much in common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where rulers and ruled have nothing in common, friendship is absent (analogy: artisan and tool). Justice/commonality is a precondition for widespread friendship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friendship of advantage prone to fault-finding
rubrics_metrics.description: Fault-finding and blame arise most naturally in friendships whose motive is utility because requirements continually enlarge and parties feel entitled to more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility-based friendships often lead to disputes over what each is owed; doers cannot meet ever-increasing demands of receivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal vs Moral friendship obligations (in advantage-based friendships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Friendship because of advantage is of two kinds: the Legal (specified conditions, clear obligations) and the Moral (unspecified expectations where giver expects an equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal obligations admit no dispute and may be non-actionable in law in some countries; Moral obligations create quarrels when expectations differ from actual discharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for measuring requital: receiver's benefit vs doer's intention
rubrics_metrics.description: A dispute: should requital be measured by the advantage conferred on the receiver or by the kind intention/quality of the doer?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aristotle suggests that for utility-based friendship the receiver's advantage is the proper standard (because the receiver is the one served); for goodness-based friendships the doer's motive is the proper standard (virtue depends on motive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who fixes the rate when no stipulation exists
rubrics_metrics.description: When no stipulation as to services is made, the question arises whether the giver or the receiver fixes the 'rate' or value of the benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If original giving was gratuitous/disinterested, the giver typically will not raise the question; where giving was avowedly for return, requital should be proportionate and, when agreement is impossible, the receiver fixing the value is seen as fair because the trusted party must accept discharge in the spirit it was contracted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requital priority: discharging debt vs unsolicited kindness
rubrics_metrics.description: The requital of benefits (discharging an obligation) is generally a higher duty than doing unsolicited kindnesses to companions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, exceptions exist when giving is more honourable or necessary (e.g., ransoming duties); claims must be weighed by amount and honour/necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportional rewards for unequal friends: respect vs profit
rubrics_metrics.description: In unequal friendships, the superior should receive more respect (the reward of goodness), while the needy should receive more profit (aid of need); equality is achieved by assigning different kinds of returns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors political practice: honour goes to those who benefit the public; money goes to those who can be paid. Friendship requires what is possible, not what is strictly due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits and nature of filial and other specific duties/honours
rubrics_metrics.description: One ought to assist parents in preference to others and pay honour to parents (but not all kinds of honour; types differ by role). Elders deserve marks of respect (rising, giving way), companions deserve frankness and participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discriminate what belongs to each relation regarding nearness, goodness, intimacy; obligations are not identical across relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissolution of friendships when qualities change
rubrics_metrics.description: It is proper to dissolve friendships whose motives (utility or pleasure) no longer apply; deception (pretending virtue) is blameworthy, and breaking off friendship with incurably depraved persons is permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is hope of moral amendment, friends have a duty to aid moral repair; where change is not extreme, past intimacy may justify some continued allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kindly Feeling vs Friendship distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Kindly Feeling (benevolence) resembles but is not identical with Friendship: it can exist toward those who do not know it, lacks intensity/yearning and need not involve intimacy or action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kindly Feeling may be the starting point of Friendship (a dormant stage), but true friendship involves reciprocal action and often arises from goodness/amiability rather than interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of Sentiment (action-oriented agreement) as component of Friendship
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity of Sentiment is connected with Friendship; it is not mere Unity of Opinion (e.g., agreement on astronomical points), but agreement on matters of action and common, important expediencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communities show Unity of Sentiment when they agree on practical collective choices (magistrates, alliances) and carry out shared decisions; such unity supports communal friendship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friendship as extension of self-love and likeness to self
rubrics_metrics.description: Friendly feelings are grounded in the feelings one has toward oneself: a friend is 'one who intends and does what is good to another for that other's sake'—the good man has such feelings toward himself and thus toward another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The good man's unity of self, continuity of pleasures and recollections, and desire for his own good make him capable of friendship; the wicked, divided in themselves, cannot be proper friends even to themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and shared life as tests and enforcers of friendship
rubrics_metrics.description: Length of time, upbringing together, and opportunities to prove one another strengthen friendship and provide secure grounds for mutual reliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors explain why brothers, those raised together, or long companions form stronger and more tested friendships than more casual associates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint over mismatched expectations in love/romantic friendship
rubrics_metrics.description: In romantic/love friendships disputes arise when lovers have different objects (pleasure vs utility) or when promises made (e.g., by a suitor) are not kept; such friendships suffer when motives and expectations are mismatched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When value cannot be equated (e.g., pleasure vs money), clarity of expectations and mutual understanding of intended ends prevent unfair dealings.
